topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session's learning outcomes and contextualises the upcoming material on cancer genetics and cellular transformation.

topics.label: Discovery of oncogenes and cell transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and establish the laboratory assays used to detect oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of cancer genes and explore how mutations in key regulators like Rb and p53 disrupt normal cellular control.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the origins and consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability, highlighting defects in DNA repair pathways, replication, and mitosis.

topics.label: Multistep tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how mutations accumulate sequentially during cancer progression and how inherited genetic defects accelerate this multi-step pathway to malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, suggests reading materials, and outlines the subject of the upcoming lecture.
